interactions.summary: The class treats immigration as a response to falling population, and Jiang pushes back by making demographic decline itself a symptom of civilizational sickness rooted in lost mobility, narcissism, and weakened religion.

speaker_notes.note: Jiang explicitly asks the class to argue against Dante at the end of the packet, keeping the immigration thesis open to challenge rather than closing the case.

claims.claim: A student says immigration is brought in because a society's own culture no longer makes enough children to sustain itself.
Jiang says population decline is itself a symptom of decline and lists lack of social mobility, homosexuality, and narcissism as parts of that syndrome.
Jiang treats immigration as only a short-term remedy for the deeper problem of civilizational decline.
Students add that rising child costs and loss of religion can also explain why young people stop forming families.

signature_moments.moment: Immigration is recast as a temporary patch on a society that has already stopped reproducing itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: immigration is just a short-term remedy
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This line ties the demographic, cultural, and moral arguments together in one causal hierarchy.

chronology_notes.note: The decline argument becomes explicitly demographic here: low fertility is treated as evidence of a society already spiritually and socially weakened.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang's bundled causes for population decline are broad and contestable; keep them as a dated lecture diagnosis rather than decontextualized factual claims.
